source.title: The Platonic Brain: Representational Convergence in EEG Foundation Models
source.authors: Nicolas Waehner; Enzo Tagliazucchi; Jacobo D. Sitt; Demian Wassermann; G. Marraffini; Trinidad Borrell

record.tranche_reason: Tests representational convergence with mKNN and CKA alignment measures and a task-free capability measure, in EEG foundation models, with a temporal-shift null calibration.
record.gate_note: The paper reports alignment-versus-capability and alignment-versus-size results. Its reported NICE marker scores are capability measurements, not standalone convergence outcomes; the individual scores are not catalogued separately. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: Tests convergence with capability and size in a new setting: EEG foundation models, including comparisons with vision and language models. It also tests sensitivity to similarity metric and temporal-null calibration.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors support convergence with NICE decodability across EEG families, leave convergence with scale open, and report metric- and modality-dependent cross-modal results. They explicitly treat the semantic interpretation as untested and caution that temporal smoothness contributes to apparent alignment.
record.recipe_differences: Measures alignment with mKNN and linear CKA, and calibrates it using circular shifts to preserve temporal smoothness. Uses NICE marker decodability as capability and treats parameter count separately; applies the analysis to EEG foundation models and EEG-to-vision/language comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The association differs by metric (mKNN versus CKA) and modality (language versus vision). Circular-shift calibration removes much of the apparent raw size trend in FEMBA–DINOv2 mKNN. The study also uses differing model-specific time windows and reports results on a single dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-family EEG alignment exceeds the cyclic null for 78/78 mKNN and 75/78 CKA comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained EEG model families exhibit detectable representational alignment, irrespective of a capability or scale trend.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix H reports that raw vision/language-model alignment to fMRI changes with size while the temporal null closely tracks it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Apparent model-to-biological-brain alignment trends can reflect temporal smoothness; biological fMRI representations are outside the specified model-to-model versions.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Workshop: Foundation Models for the Brain and Body
record.problems: Only 14 EEG models from five families and six participants; analyses use one dataset. Cross-modal neighbourhood alignment exceeded the time-shifted control only modestly. The paper notes that within-family size comparisons are confounded by shared architectures and training data. Several reported associations are qualitative, without correlation coefficients or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Individual model NICE marker R2 values and the per-marker results in Appendix D were not extracted as separate rows because they are capability measurements rather than separate alignment outcomes. The paper's raw cross-family mKNN and CKA values in Table 1 were also not recorded model by model; the reported aggregate capability associations and pairwise null-test counts are included instead.

untested.parts: Broad capability beyond NICE decodability, larger EEG scale ranges, and convergence when both cross-modal partners improve are untested.
No direct vision-language comparison on paired images and captions, or test of improvement in both modalities.
No controlled comparisons across random initializations.
No mapping, stitching, representation substitution or transfer-loss experiment.
No recurring interpretable model features or circuits are identified.
No neighbourhood-size sweep, systematic input comparison or out-of-distribution test. Layer-pair selection is calibrated but not independently varied.
No plateau over an extended scale range or experimental isolation of shared training data and objectives. Temporal smoothness is examined as another contributor.

record.verdict_notes: V2 does not cover EEG-to-vision or EEG-to-language comparisons. Those comparisons bear on the broader V1. Statistical significance above a null does not imply near-complete convergence. Figure values unavailable in the supplied text were not inferred.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish convergence across all modalities, model types, or ranges of scale. Parameter count is assessed in a limited EEG model set; capability is measured only as NICE decodability.
Does not compare vision-model representations directly with language-model representations of paired images and captions, or test whether both models' capabilities predict their alignment.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different random initializations or analysis of shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No test for recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
Tests mKNN at k = 5 and linear CKA, with a cyclic-shift null and the study's chosen data/windows. Does not sweep k or systematically compare other datasets or out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports incomplete cross-modal alignment and evidence that temporal smoothness contributes to scores. Does not experimentally isolate shared training data or objectives as causes.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Several rows need version-specific states; positive capability evidence concerns NICE decodability, and temporal smoothness remains a possible contributor rather than a proven explanation of all alignment.

statements.correction: Cross-modal capability analyses vary EEG NICE decodability and average alignment across partner-family sizes. Section 4 explicitly leaves EEG convergence with scale per se open. Joint improvement of both partners is not directly tested.
